subject: Time-varying adjacency matrix in spatio-temporal models?

messages.author: 659179b11b955d52
messages.subject: Time-varying adjacency matrix in spatio-temporal models?
parts:
Hello everyone,

Let's consider 10 animals which body mass, status (whether they are healthy or not) and hair thickness is recorded over time. These animals are connected to each other by social interactions which also vary over time and which we used to build several adjacency matrices. The variables "hair thickness" and "body mass" are time series and between-individuals correlation is partially driven by social interactions and how they vary over time (time-varying adjacency matrices).

Going through several tutorials I have found a way to specify time-varying spatial points (based on X and Y coordinates) in SPDE models by grouping the points according to the time variable. However, I could not find a way to build an SPDE model relying on adjacency matrices so I thought of using Besag models instead. 

Is there a way to specify BESAG models that my adjacency structure is varying over time with INLA? If yes, can anyone provide me with either a piece of code?

Thank you,
Camille

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Time-varying adjacency matrix in spatio-temporal models?
parts:
Hi,

In this case, I already know the graph at each time point. I would like to know if there is a way to take the structure of the social interactions into account when fitting a model to my data, for instance under the form of a random effect.

Let's say I want to know if the "health status" of an individual (ill or healthy) has an impact on its "hair thickness" and for some reason, I expect it to be affected by how individuals interact with each other around food patches. An animal well socialized has access to the patch more easily than more isolated animals, and alimentation has a direct impact on fur quality. Thus, individuals that interact a lot (i.e. high weights in the adjacency matrix / close to each other in the network) are more likely to show similar patterns. To some extend, I expect this correlation to be similar to correlations found in usual spatial analysis.

In addition, the fur thickness of an individual on time t is correlated to its thickness on time t-1. So there is a temporal autocorrelation at the individual level. 

In my case, I have one measure of fur thickness per day per individual, one adjacency matrix per day and individual health status (binary, constant over time). Since the adjacency matrix is different every day, the structure of the "spatial" correlation is changing over time. For the sake of simplicity, I would consider adjacency matrices to be independent from each other (although it is not true). 

The model should thus look like this: 
thickness ~ 1 + health_status + 
                   f(Individual_ID1, time, model = rw1) + 
                   f(Individual_ID2, model = besag (?), graph = Array_of_adjacency_matrices (?), group = time etc.)


Is there any way to implement this using INLA? I have seen this kind of model with SPDE models but I cannot make an SPDE using my adjacency matrices (as far as I know).

Thank you,
C.
